chunks: And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala') from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who prays the two obligatory rak'ahs and does not sit until he bows in the third. He said: 'He completes his prayer and prostrates the two prostrations of forgetfulness while sitting before he speaks.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْمَكْتُوبَةِ: The two obligatory rak'ahs (of Fajr or Zuhr/Asr)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who forgets to sit after the second rak'ah and continues praying?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that omitting the sitting for tashahhud after the second rak'ah does not invalidate the prayer but requires sujadat al-sahw (prostrations of forgetfulness) performed while seated before speaking. This specific instruction highlights the Shia emphasis on maintaining the structural integrity of prayer through corrective acts rather than repetition, ensuring the worshipper’s focus remains undisturbed by minor errors.
